t: The kingdom of Saul, David and Solomon, known chiefly from the Hebrew Bible, with its scale debated by historians and archaeologists.
David made Jerusalem the capital and Solomon built its temple, making the city a political and religious centre.
Its memory as a golden age shaped Jewish, Christian and Islamic ideas of kingship and messianic hope.
dyk: The earliest reference to the “House of David” outside the Bible appears on the Tel Dan stele, an Aramaic inscription found in northern Israel in 1993.
ev: Saul is anointed king by Samuel (traditional chronology)
Saul is killed by the Philistines at the Battle of Mount Gilboa
David captures Jerusalem and makes it his capital
Solomon succeeds David after a struggle with his brother Adonijah
The Temple of Jerusalem is completed, according to the Bible
The northern tribes reject Rehoboam and the kingdom splits in two

f.successor: Kingdom of Israel; Kingdom of Judah
